The '''2002–03 [[La Liga]]''' season was the 72nd since its establishment. It began on 31 August 2002, and concluded on 22 June 2003.

== Teams ==
Twenty teams competed in the league&nbsp;– the top seventeen teams from the previous season and the three teams promoted from the [[2001–02 Segunda División|Segunda División]]. The promoted teams were [[Atlético Madrid]], [[Racing de Santander|Racing Santander]] and [[Recreativo de Huelva|Recreativo]], returning to the top flight after an absence of two, one and twenty three years respectively. They replaced [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]], [[CD Tenerife|Tenerife]] and [[Real Zaragoza|Zaragoza]] after spending time in the top flight for two, one and twenty four years respectively.

=== Fair Play award ===
Real Madrid was the winner of the Fair-play award, with 76 points; second was Real Sociedad; and third was Deportivo La Coruña.<ref name="FairPlay">{{cite web|title=Ganadores de los Premios Juego Limpio |trans-title=Fair-play awards Winners |url=http://www.rfef.es/index.jsp?nodo=298#ancla7 |publisher=[[Royal Spanish Football Federation|RFEF]] |access-date=5 September 2010 |language=es |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100407195555/http://www.rfef.es/index.jsp?nodo=298 |archive-date=7 April 2010 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=El Real Madrid, ganador del Premio al Juego Limpio 2003 |trans-title=Real Madrid, 2003 Fair Play Award Winner |url=http://www.noticias.info/Archivo/2003/200306/20030626/20030626_6350.shtm |publisher=[[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]] (filed) |access-date=6 September 2010 |language=es |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110807104903/http://www.noticias.info/Archivo/2003/200306/20030626/20030626_6350.shtm |archive-date=7 August 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
